anti_overlap: Does not adjudicate whether the register audit's classification of any specific country, aggregate, or historical/disputed code is factually correct — that is fd-geopolitical-entity-provenance's territory.

Does not evaluate whether individual task steps are unambiguous, executable prose for a weaker model, or whether the plan's f-NNN citations accurately restate what the brainstorm/melange source documents actually say — that is fd-planexec-authority-traceability's territory.

Does not assess sourcing/citation adequacy, staleness rules, or named-person risk-tiering for the issue or institution corpus content itself — flag only where evidence *about* that content (e.g. its hash coverage) is missing, not whether the content is well-sourced.
decision_lens: A finding earns attention when the referee protocol could return PASS (or a green <verify> block, or a satisfied Acceptance Criterion check) while the underlying determinism or data-plane-visibility claim it is supposed to certify is actually false or has become untestable — trace what each PASS/FAIL signal in this plan actually proves versus what the plan's prose claims it proves, one signal at a time.
focus: Whether the rung-0 referee protocol itself — the re-baselining move to strabo-r0-baseline, the R1 code-leg and new R1-data-leg (data_manifest hashing), and the multi-seed R2 replay statements per task — actually produces sound, non-gameable evidence that flag-off behavior is unchanged and flag-on behavior is deterministic, rather than a protocol whose PASS signal quietly stops meaning what the plan claims it means partway through the rung.
name: fd-refereeharness-rebaseline-integrity
persona: Apply the perspective of a reproducibility/determinism-testing engineer who has spent years building golden-master and replay-based regression harnesses for simulation and financial-modeling systems — someone who treats a referee protocol as a piece of software with its own correctness requirements, and who reflexively asks of any PASS/FAIL gate: what exactly does this certify, what would a false PASS look like, and where does this harness's own blind spot move when the ground truth it compares against is deliberately allowed to shift underneath it.
review_areas: Whether the referee's discriminating power survives Wave B: Task 5 tags strabo-r0-baseline once, before Task 7 intentionally changes flag-off live data (register consolidation); verify whether Tasks 8-17's R1-data-leg comparisons against that single frozen baseline can still distinguish 'the disclosed Task-7 delta' from a genuinely new, accidental data-plane regression introduced by any later task, or whether the manifest-diff becomes permanently 'different, disclosed' and loses discriminating power for the rest of the rung.

Whether data_manifest (Task 2) actually gets extended to hash every file later waves make load-bearing — specifically roster-2025.yaml (Task 9) and the v1 issue-roster file (Tasks 13-14) — or whether those are introduced through a path that isn't embed-only / isn't in the hashed set, silently recreating the exact blindness class Task 2 exists to close.

Whether referee.sh's actual current CLI and output contract (it reportedly takes a mandatory <old-commit> positional with no default) matches every task's assumed invocation and matches Acceptance Criterion 9's `grep -q "R1.*PASS"` check closely enough that the check can't be satisfied by output that isn't actually a genuine pass.

Whether the InstitutionStore HashMap->FxHashMap fix (Task 3) is the only place in code the plan touches where iteration-order or other hash-based nondeterminism could recur, and whether any Wave A-C task risks perturbing the BenchOperative cadre's draw-order-fragile determinism lock (procgen_cast_golden_pin) without the plan ever re-asserting that regression pin.

Whether each task's per-task R2 statement (seeds 1000/2000, or 'no new keyed state') is calibrated to the actual amount of new keyed state the task introduces, and whether the FINDINGS-GATE: PASS|FAIL line Task 3 introduces is consistently wired into every later task and Acceptance Criterion that needs it, rather than only appearing once.

Whether Task 4's ts-rs fix verification (`test ! -d crates/packages`) is strong enough to prove regeneration lands correctly from both invocation contexts the task's own Steps describe, or whether it only proves the stray tree was deleted once.

severity_examples.condition: Trace what strabo-r0-baseline's R1-data-leg comparison actually proves for any task after Task 7, given Task 7's own disclosed manifest delta.
severity_examples.scenario: strabo-r0-baseline is tagged once in Task 5, and Task 7's live-data consolidation is an intended, disclosed divergence from it; but Tasks 8-17's R1-data-leg still diffs unconditionally against that same frozen manifest with no accounting for the already-disclosed Task-7 delta, so the referee's FAIL signal for a genuinely new accidental data regression introduced in, say, Task 13's situation feed becomes indistinguishable from the already-known Task-7 diff — the rung's central 'referee sees the data plane' claim (f-031's whole reason for existing) silently stops discriminating starting at Wave B, and no <verify> block or Acceptance Criterion in the plan catches that.

severity_examples.condition: Check whether every file made load-bearing by Waves C and D is named in Task 2's data_manifest population step, or only the files that existed when Task 2 was written.
severity_examples.scenario: Task 2 hashes include_str!-embedded bytes for baseline GDP, country-map, and issue registry ('when it exists'), but Task 9's roster-2025.yaml and the v1 issue-roster file from Tasks 13-14 are introduced without an explicit instruction to add them to the hashed data_manifest set, so a post-ship edit to the roster file could be as invisible to the R1-data leg as the pre-Task-2 GDP baseline was.

severity_examples.condition: Confirm whether Task 1 or Task 3's changes could plausibly alter draw order consumed by generate_cadre, and whether the plan's suite run would actually execute the golden-pin test.
severity_examples.scenario: No task in Waves A-C re-runs or even names procgen_cast_golden_pin, despite Task 1 and Task 3 touching the same institution-store/GDP code paths the melange synthesis flags as adjacent to generate_cadre's draw-order-fragile contract (f-033/f-036) — a scope-blind reflow there is explicitly undetectable by either R1 or R2, yet nothing in this plan's referee protocol adds a check for it.

source_domain: deterministic-simulation reproducibility engineering / golden-master and replay-based regression harness design
success_hints: Named the exact task pair or wave boundary where the re-baselining protocol's discriminating power degrades, with the specific mechanism (frozen single-tag baseline vs. an intentionally-diverging data plane).
Traced whether every file a later wave makes load-bearing is actually inside Task 2's hashed data_manifest set, file by file, rather than asserting the general claim once.
Checked referee.sh's actual current CLI/output contract against the plan's assumed invocations and verify-block greps, ideally by reading the script rather than trusting the plan's paraphrase of it.
Found at least one concrete class of iteration-order/determinism risk the plan's instrument repairs don't cover, naming the specific code path.
Distinguished 'R1 passes and R2 passes' from 'the artifact actually proved what the acceptance criterion claims' at least once, with a concrete counter-scenario.
task_context: Find what makes this rung-0 plan fail and what it's missing: as an execution-grade plan for a weaker executor, do its tasks, verify blocks, and referee protocol actually deliver refereed real-world grounding, and where does it silently contradict the brainstorm Amendments, the melange prescriptions it claims to encode, or the codebase as it exists? Ground findings specifically in the referee-protocol mechanics: the single strabo-r0-baseline tag (Task 5) frozen before Wave B's intentionally-diverging data change (Task 7), the data_manifest hash's actual coverage of files introduced by later waves (roster-2025.yaml in Task 9, the v1 issue roster in Tasks 13-14), the referee.sh CLI/output contract assumed by every task and Acceptance Criterion 9's grep check, the FxHashMap/iteration-order determinism fix's scope versus the same defect family elsewhere in code the plan touches (including whether procgen_cast_golden_pin or an equivalent cadre-determinism check is ever re-asserted), and whether each task's stated R2 statement is strong enough given what 'a single-seed certificate certifies' (f-046).
